classification.difficultyReason: Eliminate the parameter and sketch a line, vertical parabolas and a sideways parabola.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of the following parametric equations, where $t\in\mathbb{R}$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}t&=x-1\\y&=3(x-1)\\y&=3x-3\end{align*}$$
Since $t\in\mathbb{R}$, the entire line is described. Its intercepts are $(1,0)$ and $(0,-3)$.

spec.description: Complete straight line with arrows at both ends; black axes and ticks at x=1 and y=−3.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution-only; no graph is supplied in the student prompt.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}t&=x+1\\y&=(x+1)^2\end{align*}$$
Since $t\in\mathbb{R}$, the entire upward-opening parabola is described. Its vertex is $(-1,0)$ and its $y$-intercept is $(0,1)$.

spec.description: Correct upward-opening parabola with vertex (−1,0), rather than the inconsistent answer-key graph.
spec.mathematics: x=t−1, y=t² gives y=(x+1)²; all real x.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}t&=2x\\y&=\frac{(2x)^2}{4}-2x\\y&=(x-1)^2-1\end{align*}$$
The entire parabola is described. Its vertex is $(1,-1)$ and its $x$-intercepts are $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$.

spec.description: Upward parabola crossing the origin and (2,0), with vertex (1,−1); both branches continue.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}t&=2y\\x&=(2y)^2-1\\x&=4y^2-1\end{align*}$$
Since $t\in\mathbb{R}$, both branches are described. The vertex is $(-1,0)$; setting $x=0$ gives $y=\pm\frac12$.

spec.description: Right-opening parabola with two continuing branches, vertex (−1,0), and marked axis values ±1/2.
spec.mathematics: x=4y²−1 for all real y; x≥−1.
